changes: Add a secret-safe dual-instance E2E driver that opens authenticated zsh and x570 sessions plus live /api/events.mux WebSockets, keeps the original zsh socket open, and performs the x570 outage, recovery, and token-rotation sequence without logging bearer values or cookies.
tests: On the live deployment, assert zsh protected HTTP is 200 and the same zsh WebSocket completes request/response round trips before, during, and after x570 stop, recovery, and rotation; retain x570 503, recovery 200, old-cookie 401, old-WebSocket close, and new-session/WebSocket checks.
docs: Document the redacted concurrent isolation check and the rule that root HTTP 200 is not sufficient health evidence.
evidence: A redacted E2E result bound to the successor deployment identity, recording only status codes, WebSocket round-trip outcomes, and state transitions.

changes: Upgrade Hub deployment receipts to a versioned, secret-free pre/post manifest that captures regular files, symlinks, directories, uid/gid/mode, managed group pre-state, cron and monitoring files, and the complete certificate lineage paths needed for exact restoration.

Store metadata-preserving backups for every pre-existing managed object, record receipt SHA-256 and predecessor/current state identities, chain-guard rollback, restore or remove every managed object in dependency-safe order, and record a verified rollback result.
tests: Fixture tests cover apply/rollback when certificate lineage, group, directories, cron, and managed files are absent and when each pre-exists with nondefault content and metadata; compare complete normalized pre/post manifests byte-for-byte and metadata-for-metadata.
Run a real VPS apply/rollback/reapply canary, verify the rollback manifest equals the captured pre-state, and preserve zsh availability throughout.
docs: Document receipt schema/location/hash, exact restore ordering, chain guards, automatic versus manual rollback, and the real rollback verification procedure.
evidence: Successor deployment evidence binds the package hash, deployed receipt hash, pre/post manifest identities, real rollback result, and final reapplied identity.

changes: Refactor install-dsh-node.sh into a locked, receipt-driven installer that stages immutable version/config generations, validates them before activation, and atomically switches stable active pointers used by the launcher and fixed DSH_HOME.

Capture the complete managed pre-state including content hashes, uid/gid/mode, symlinks, launcher, settings, and credentials; restore it on every failed phase and expose an explicit chain-guarded rollback command while leaving legacy ~/.dsh outside managed scope.
tests: Add isolated shell integration tests for first install and managed rerun with injected failure after each mutation/activation phase, asserting exact pre-state hashes, metadata, pointers, and absence of mixed releases; also test successful upgrade and explicit rollback.
docs: Document versioned release/config layout, stable launcher behavior, receipt location, upgrade procedure, explicit rollback, and preserved legacy/session boundaries.
evidence: Local failure-injection matrix plus x570 managed rerun and rollback/reapply evidence showing rc.6, fixed Home, 0600 configuration, unchanged legacy ~/.dsh, and the approved model roster.

changes: Make the instance installer require an active lingering user manager before enabling its user unit, with an explicit --enable-linger setup path that performs and verifies the authorized host change; fail preflight without either existing linger or that flag.
Record linger and unit pre-state in the node receipt so rollback restores the previous lifecycle state without changing unrelated users.
tests: Add command-fixture tests for linger already enabled, missing linger rejection, authorized enablement, enablement failure, and rollback to prior state.

On x570, verify the unit and reverse tunnel survive termination of the interactive SSH session and recover after an authorized reboot, with the endpoint returning authenticated HTTP/WebSocket traffic.
docs: Document why linger is required, the explicit enablement command, logout/reboot verification, and rollback behavior.
evidence: Redacted x570 loginctl/unit state plus post-logout and post-reboot tunnel/endpoint results bound to the successor node and deployment identities.

changes: Serialize Hub apply/rollback/add/remove/status-recovery operations with one inter-process lock acquired before registry read and held through validation, reload, receipt commit, and cleanup.

Stage registry and routes as one identified generation, embed and verify the same generation ID in both files, maintain a durable pending/committed transaction marker, and recover interrupted transactions deterministically before any new mutator.
Persist pre/post registry and route files, hashes, metadata, chain identities, and socket quarantine metadata in transaction receipts; add a chain-guarded transaction rollback command.

For removal, atomically quarantine a stale or forced-live socket before activation, restore the same inode/path/metadata on failure, retain the quarantine through commit for reversible rollback, and only garbage-collect it after its receipt is no longer reversible.
tests: Deterministic multi-process add/add and add/remove tests prove no lost IDs.
Failure and process-kill injection after each durable boundary proves recovery selects one complete generation and registry/routes IDs always match.

Stale and forced-live socket failure tests prove exact path, inode type, owner/group/mode, registry, and routes pre-state restoration; completed add/remove rollback tests verify chain guards and exact reversal.
docs: Document lock scope, transaction receipt/chain model, crash recovery, socket quarantine, --force limitations, rollback order, and garbage-collection rules.
evidence: Concurrency/failure-injection suite results and real VPS add/remove/rollback canary bound to generation and receipt hashes.

changes: Replace mutable certificate image tags in issuance, renewal, and deletion paths with one allowlisted certbot/dns-cloudflare image reference pinned by sha256 digest; validate the reference before exposing the mode-0600 credential mount and include the digest in receipts/status.
tests: Reject tag-only and malformed image references, assert every certificate command uses the same digest, and run production-image issuance/renewal/deletion canaries with credential-redacted output.
docs: Document the pinned image identity, controlled digest update procedure, and verification command.
evidence: Package tests plus VPS image inspection and renewal canary bind the exact digest without exposing Cloudflare credential contents.

changes: Expose the clean-node installer as a packaged command and align README and the VPS runbook with the implemented Hub apply/status/renewal/rollback/transaction/node commands.
tests: Add documentation command-contract tests that resolve every packaged invocation, parse every shown option, and check renewal schedule, receipt paths, rollback chain, socket handling, monitoring, and clean-node bootstrap against generated/runtime values.
docs: Replace legacy-only renewal text with the DNS-01 Hub workflow; include exact commands, receipt paths, rollback ordering, tunnel stop, --force semantics, stale socket recovery, clean-node install, linger, verification, and incident steps.
evidence: Passing command-contract tests and a package manifest proving both edge and node installer entry points ship and execute.

changes: Expand Hub status into explicit configured and ready invariants: registry/routes generation equality, registry and managed-file modes/ownership, all required Compose mounts/group_add, socket-directory metadata, Nginx worker group membership, pinned certificate identity/validity, renewal/health schedules, and functional Nginx validation.

Classify each registered instance as online, offline, insecure, or missing using lstat, exact owner/group/mode, a bounded Unix-socket connect probe, and a bounded functional HTTPS request through that instance's Nginx route to a protected gateway endpoint; online requires the expected gateway 401 response, while a listening but nonresponsive socket is offline.

Install a secret-free systemd health service/timer covering public route, functional gateway, service/socket, and certificate checks. Attach an OnFailure alert unit that writes a mode-0600 persistent alarm record, emits to the journal, and uses wall as the installed delivery consumer for logged-in operator terminals; include service/timer/alert and retention files in deployment rollback manifests.

Install bounded journald/log retention for the Hub units and document that wall is the immediate on-host delivery path while the persistent failed-unit/alarm record is the catch-up path for operators who were not logged in; do not claim unconfigured Tencent Cloud account-side alert delivery.
tests: Add status corruption tests for generation mismatch, missing mounts, wrong registry/socket-directory metadata, absent group membership, broken renewal/health schedules, and certificate identity mismatch.

Add socket-state tests for listening-and-responsive, listening-but-nonresponsive, stale, missing, wrong-owner, wrong-mode, and regular-file paths, asserting that readiness requires the functional protected-route 401 response.

On the VPS keep an SSH TTY open, inject a synthetic health failure, prove the OnFailure unit records it and wall delivers the alert text to that operator terminal, then clear the synthetic condition and prove the timer returns healthy.
docs: Define configured versus ready, every per-instance state, protected-route probe semantics, scheduled check cadence, systemd OnFailure to persistent alarm/journal/wall delivery, operator catch-up and acknowledgement steps, optional Tencent Cloud integration as explicitly unconfigured, and retention limits.
evidence: Corruption/state test matrix and fresh successor deployment status showing Hub configured, x570 online/ready through the protected-route probe, zsh healthy, pinned certificate valid, monitoring installed, and one synthetic alert observed on an operator SSH TTY with no credential data.
